messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Model averaging
messages.body_plain:
For anybody who might be interested in this in the future, I figured out why the weighted output wouldn't plot correctly, and it was user error on my end (I gave the wrong "tipranges"). With that fixed, the weighted average output plots as expected.

On Wednesday, November 13, 2019 at 3:26:49 PM UTC-5, Jack Boyle wrote:
> Thanks, Nick!
>
> On Thursday, November 7, 2019 at 6:11:07 PM UTC-5, Nick Matzke wrote:
> > Hi!
> >
> > On Fri, Nov 8, 2019 at 11:59 AM Jack Boyle <john....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi, I'm new to BioGeoBears, but so far it's been very easy to get into--thanks for all of the documentation, it's great!
> > >
> > > I've been working my way through the analyses displayed in the getting started script (http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script), and I've found two models with good AIC support. I'm interested in doing model averaging using the AIC weights.
> > >
> > > It seems like I ought to be able to do something like this:
> > >
> > > weighted_table = results_model_1$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node * model_weight_1 + results_model_2$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node * model_weight_2
> > >
> > > I wasn't quite sure how to plot the resulting model averages, though, so I tried getting clever:
> > >
> > > results_weighted = results_model_1
> > > results_weighted$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node = weighted_table
> > > plot_BioGeoBEARS_results(results_weighted, ...)
> > >
> > > This produced a figure with pie charts and all that was colored in a very reasonable way, except that the colors all corresponded to the wrong ranges, and the tips were mislabelled. This made me nervous that perhaps the order of columns in the two tables from results_model_1 and results_model_2 were perhaps not the same, although some digging made it seem like they probably were?
> > >
> > > Anyway, two main questions:
> > >
> > > 1) Is it possible to weight models the way I did, or am I misunderstanding how the results are stored in the biogeobears output?
> >
> > Yes, that code you have should work fine.  The only assumption is that results_model_1 and results_model_2 used the same input tree and geography files (and same max-number of ranges etc.)
> >
> > In the res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node table,
> >
> > rows = nodes, with the tip nodes first, then the root node, then the internal nodes (same order as the APE tree object, used prt(tr) to see the nodes table
> >
> > columns = states/ranges
> >
> > So, do
> >
> > dim(results_model_1$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node)
> > dim(results_model_2$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node)
> >
> > ...to check that they actually have the same # of nodes and ranges.
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Nick
> >
> > PS to make sure the resulting model-weighted probabilities add up to 1, rescale model_weight_1 and model_weight_2 so that they add up to 1 (if they don't already).
> >
> > Cheers,
> > Nick
> >
> >
> >
> >
> >
> > > 2) If it is possible, do you have any recommendations for plotting a weighted model that doesn't shuffle around tip values, colors, etc?
> > >
> > > Thanks for the help!
> > > Jack
> > >

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Help with a BIogeobears scenario
messages.body_plain:
Hi- a key issue is to be clear on what the parameters mean.

Eg “d” is the rate of range-expansion dispersal, not the “range”.

The “j” parameter is the relative weight of jump dispersal - discussed in detail on PhyloWiki (google it)

Both “d” and “j” events can be short-distance or long-distance dispersal, it depends only on the distance between areas. Although, to make a gross generalization, probably j events are more often long-distance events than d-events.

To actually measure the effect of geographic distance on dispersal, use a +x model variant, see eg Van Dam and Matzke 2016, J Biogeographic.

To actually get a probabilistic sample of possible exact dispersal histories, which you could manually classify into short or long distance based on a distance cutoff, use Biogeographic Stochastic Mapping, see Dupin, Matzke et al 2017, J Biogeog.

Cheers,
Nick

On Sunday, December 15, 2019, Adam Rick Bessa <adamri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I would like to ask everyone's help to understand a scenario.
> I have a biogeographic scenario in which the groups with reduced genetic divergence are separated by the Andes.
>
> Biogeobears analysis indicated two models as the best fit to our data (DEC + J and DIVALIKE + J), with DIVALIKE + J being the best supported model (attached). Estimates of parameters d (dispersal range), e (extinction) and j founder-event show a greater support tendency for parameter j (founder-event or jump-dispersal). However, my other analysis (ABC and IMa) show clear support for a long-dispersal distance scenario, which would be at odds with Biogeobears-supported jump-dispersal (j).
>
> The distribution of probabilities for the parameters d (range dispersal), e (extinction) and  (founder-event) indicate that the analysis was difficult to recover the long-distance dispersal recovered by other analysis (ABC and IMa)?
>
> If this is true, what could explain this contradiction of Biogeobears with ABC and IMa? Is there any technical question for this?
>
> Just to help the debate. The group studied occurs from South America to Central America. However, I do not have a representative sampling of species distribution, mainly near the mountain range where, which is somewhat vicarious for this group. Is there any relationship of incomplete sampling of species in the Biogeobears analysis?
>
>
>
> Thank you for your contribution,
>
>
> Best,
>
> Adam Bessa
